config.title: useReducer vs useState

intro.title: useReducer vs useState
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple counter application twice—first using Vue's `ref` (similar to React's `useState`) and then using a custom `useReducer` function—to compare two state management approaches. You will learn the core concept of state management, focusing on when to use simple reactive state versus a reducer pattern for more complex logic. The main technologies involved are Vue 3's Composition API with `ref`, `computed`, and custom composable functions. By the end, you'll understand how `useReducer` centralizes state updates through actions, making your code more predictable and maintainable for certain use cases compared to `ref`.
intro.usecase: In real Vue applications, managing complex component state is crucial for features like multi-step forms, shopping carts, or dashboard controls. For example, an e-commerce checkout form with shipping options, payment methods, and promo codes requires coordinated state updates that useState alone can make messy. useReducer provides a cleaner solution for these scenarios by centralizing state logic, similar to how Vuex handles application-wide state but at the component level. This pattern appears in admin panels with filter systems, interactive data visualizations, and any UI where multiple actions affect the same state object.

objectives: Implement a Vue component using useState for managing simple counter state
Construct a Vue component using useReducer to handle complex state transitions
Configure a reducer function that processes different action types for state updates
Apply useState for independent state values and useReducer for related state logic
Initialize both useState and useReducer hooks with appropriate default values
Manipulate component state by dispatching actions to a reducer
Render UI elements that display state values from both useState and useReducer

steps.title: Add buttons for useReducer actions
steps.instruction: Add three buttons to dispatch INCREMENT, DECREMENT, and RESET actions to the reducer. Use @click binding to call dispatch with the appropriate action object.
steps.hint: Create three button elements with @click handlers that call dispatch({ type: 'ACTION_TYPE' }). Add them after the existing useReducer counter display.

<button @click="dispatch({ type: 'INCREMENT' })">Increment</button>
<button @click="dispatch({ type: 'DECREMENT' })">Decrement</button>
<button @click="dispatch({ type: 'RESET' })">Reset</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The useReducer counter section now has three buttons: Increment, Decrement, and Reset, each wired to dispatch the corresponding action.
successCriteria: Three buttons are added with @click handlers that dispatch INCREMENT, DECREMENT, and RESET actions.
